name: Microsoft Azure
tagline: Cloud APIs, Azure CLI, identity, DevOps, and AI services.
shortDescription: Azure exposes ARM APIs, Azure CLI, SDKs, resource groups, managed identities, and extensive cloud service docs.
agentSummary: Agents can inspect and manage Azure resources through CLI/API with resource group, subscription, and RBAC boundaries.
bestFor: Enterprise cloud operations, Azure AI, Functions, Container Apps, storage, and DevOps.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Subscription-wide permissions, Entra ID, networking, and billing need strict guardrails. Model behavior, costs, rate limits, data retention, and safety policies can change by model and account tier; use evals, spend caps, and data controls for sensitive workloads. MCP servers inherit the connected account's scopes and may send prompts or data to third-party services; configure read-only or narrow scopes when available. CLI access is powerful but can run destructive local or production commands; prefer dry runs, preview environments, and non-production credentials.
pricingSummary: Public per-service pricing and calculator; enterprise discounts can vary.
authModel: Entra ID, service principals, managed identities, RBAC, and CLI login.
accountCreation: Self-serve signup with billing and identity verification.
browserSupport: Portal is useful for IAM, monitoring, and billing review.

capabilities.detail: Azure CLI covers resource and service management.
Azure REST APIs and ARM resource APIs are documented.
Microsoft's Azure MCP Server connects agent clients to Azure services and resources through Azure credentials.
Microsoft Learn provides service docs, API refs, and CLI refs.
Public per-service pricing and calculator; enterprise discounts can vary.
Self-serve signup with billing and identity verification.
Portal is useful for IAM, monitoring, and billing review.
The tool has documented test, local, preview, self-hosted, or staging paths that let agents validate changes away from production.
